title: When someone falls behind
sub: Film 3 of Ownership and performance, in Leading data people: when one person's work falls behind the team's. Find the cause before you judge: training, fit for the role, or a hard time. Clear what's in the way, measure the gap against the team's own change, and give it time.
howto: The film is drawn in ink line: flat colour with one even dark line, and whole people in the places where they work and meet, at a car plant in Fremont from 1982 and at the university. Its ideas are written by hand: at a board, where a consultant explains them to the university's managers, and in notebooks, where Tomás writes his plan and Helena keeps what to remember. Its colours mean the same in every film: blue is a question, a plan or a rule (the books' questions, Tomás's own plan), orange is data (the days from a request to first use), green something done or a blocker cleared (his Thursdays kept clear, the weeks that kept pace), and amber a risk or a gap (the gap between his work and the team's, a report sent back). People and their clothes wear none of them.
